text: Love Is Blind is a reality television franchise on Netflix created by Chris Coelen, originating in the United States and replicated in eleven countries worldwide, including Japan, Sweden, and the United Kingdom. The show presents itself as an experiment to determine whether love can develop based on personality rather than physical appearance. Contestants engage in private conversations for 10 days in purpose-built "pods," small rooms where they can speak to each other via speaker but cannot see one another, except through a blue translucent barrier that provides no visual detail. Initially paired in a speed-dating format, participants can later choose to extend their dates. A couple only meets face-to-face after one of them proposes marriage, which can be made at any time during the pod phase. Following the proposal, the engaged couples attend a one-week couples' retreat at a resort where they spend time together, experience physical intimacy for the first time, and meet the other couples in the experiment. After the retreat, the couples move into an apartment complex to live together for the final three weeks, during which they meet their partners' friends and families, discuss topics such as finances, recreation, personal habits, and preferred homes, and plan weddings to be held at the end of four weeks. During wedding planning, women shop for wedding dresses and men shop for suits, often with a few friends or family members, and also decide on the wedding cake's design and flavor. At the altar, each participant decides whether to say "I do" and get legally married. Of the 120 couples formed across all spin-offs, 48 have married, and as of August 2025, 27 of these couples are still together, resulting in a 40% success rate for marriage and a 58% chance of staying together after marriage. The series features an equal number of men and women seeking love, and the format—where suitors are chosen without visual contact—has been compared to The Dating Game. Each season concludes with a reunion special, and the U.S. format has been adapted in several countries.
